questions.stem: Cholera toxin and pertussis toxin act on opposite G proteins, yet both raise intracellular cAMP. Which pair of mechanisms is correct?

options.A: Cholera activates Gi; pertussis activates Gs
options.C: Cholera locks Gs active; pertussis blocks Gi
options.D: Cholera blocks Gq; pertussis activates PLC

questions.explanation: Cholera ADP-ribosylates Gαs (no GTPase → stays on); pertussis ADP-ribosylates Gi (can't inhibit AC). A: Reversed. B: PDE isn't the target. D: Gq and PLC aren't involved. E: Both act via G proteins, not AC directly.

questions.stem: A hormone activates a Gq-coupled receptor on a smooth muscle cell. Which second messenger directly releases Ca²⁺ from the ER?
questions.explanation: Gq activates phospholipase C, which cleaves PIP2 into IP3 and DAG; IP3 opens Ca²⁺ channels in the ER. A: DAG stays in the membrane and, with Ca²⁺, activates PKC. B: PIP3 is made by PI3-kinase and serves as a PH-domain docking site. C: cAMP is made by adenylyl cyclase (Gs). D: cGMP is made by guanylyl cyclase.
questions.source: Signal Transduction, VI slide 29; VII slides 8–9

questions.stem: After an RTK autophosphorylates, which protein links it to Ras activation by binding phosphotyrosine through an SH2 domain?
questions.explanation: Grb2 binds phosphotyrosine via SH2 and recruits SOS (a Ras GEF) via SH3. A: Raf acts downstream of Ras. B: STATs bind JAK-phosphorylated cytokine receptors. C: Smad4 is in TGF-β signaling. E: PKA is cAMP-dependent.

questions.stem: TGF-β binds its type II receptor. What is the next step in the pathway?

options.B: Type II receptor phosphorylates type I on serine

questions.explanation: TGF-β receptors are serine/threonine kinases: ligand-bound type II recruits and phosphorylates type I, which phosphorylates an R-Smad; R-Smad joins Smad4 and regulates transcription in the nucleus. A: Tyrosine autophosphorylation is RTK signaling. C: JAK is used by cytokine receptors. D: Smad4 (Co-Smad) is not phosphorylated. E: R-Smad acts in a complex with Smad4.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old boy has recurrent severe infections, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive. He has almost no circulating T cells and his thymic shadow is absent. His maternal uncle died in infancy of infections. Which gene is most likely mutated?
questions.explanation: X-linked SCID: common γ chain (IL2RG) shared by many cytokine receptors. B: ADA deficiency causes autosomal recessive SCID. C: BTK causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia (B cells absent, T cells normal). D: WAS causes eczema, thrombocytopenia, infections. E: CD40L causes hyper-IgM syndrome.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old has multiple café-au-lait macules, axillary freckling, and cutaneous neurofibromas. The defective protein normally does what?
questions.explanation: Neurofibromin (NF1) is a Ras GAP; its loss keeps Ras active. A: That's a GEF (e.g., SOS), which activates Ras. B: JAK phosphorylates STATs. C: Gi inhibits adenylyl cyclase. E: Phosphodiesterases degrade cGMP.

questions.stem: A man taking sildenafil uses nitroglycerin for chest pain and becomes severely hypotensive. Which statement explains how the two drugs together raise cGMP?

options.A: NO blocks cGMP breakdown; sildenafil activates guanylyl cyclase
options.B: NO activates adenylyl cyclase; sildenafil blocks cAMP breakdown
options.C: Both activate membrane guanylyl cyclase receptors
options.E: NO activates soluble guanylyl cyclase; sildenafil blocks cGMP breakdown

questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin supplies NO, which activates the cytoplasmic guanylyl cyclase, so more cGMP is made; sildenafil inhibits a cGMP phosphodiesterase, so less is destroyed. Together they cause excessive vasodilation. A: Reversed. B: cAMP isn't the messenger here. C: NO's receptor is the cytoplasmic guanylyl cyclase, and sildenafil acts on the phosphodiesterase. D: Only sildenafil inhibits the phosphodiesterase.

questions.stem: With continuous exposure to epinephrine, a cell's β-adrenergic response fades. Which event underlies this desensitization?

options.B: Grb2 binds phosphotyrosines on the receptor
options.C: β-ARK phosphorylates the receptor, which then binds β-arrestin
options.D: Gαs loses its intrinsic GTPase activity
options.E: PKA dissociates from its anchoring proteins

questions.explanation: β-adrenergic receptor kinase phosphorylates the receptor, creating a binding site for β-arrestin, which blocks further G protein binding; receptors are then endocytosed. A: Phosphodiesterase hydrolyzes cAMP; it isn't a kinase. B: Grb2 binds phosphotyrosines on RTKs. D: Loss of Gαs GTPase (as with cholera toxin) prolongs the signal. E: AKAPs set PKA location, not receptor sensitivity.
